justification: The opening task is substantially complete across all occupied storeys: I measured 36/26/26 doors and 46/53/49 windows on storeys 1–3, with every room having a door and every identified habitable room having an exterior window. The systemic defect is window suitability: nearly all windows have a 0.604 m sill, including guest-suite and office-like uses where the standard expects about 0.9–1.0 m, so significant repeated adjustment is needed despite otherwise strong hosting, sizing, and operation checks.
evidence: Live measurements found 88 doors and 148 windows, all 236 hosted and bounding-box-contained in their host walls; the access check found 0 doorless rooms and habitable-window coverage of 15/15 on storey 1, 15/15 on storey 2, and 17/17 on storey 3. Window bounding boxes measured 0.604 m sills throughout almost all rooms, matching the agent’s statement: “Every room people use has … casements on a 2′-0″ (0.6 m) sill.”
strengths: Complete whole-building coverage: storey 1 has 36 doors/46 windows, storey 2 has 26/53, and storey 3 has 26/49.
All 82 recorded rooms have at least one door; no floor or room-use group is missing door coverage.
Habitable-window coverage is complete by floor: 15/15 occupied rooms on floor 1, 15/15 on floor 2, and 17/17 on floor 3.
All 236 openings have wall hosts and lie within their host bounding boxes.

Opening measurements report no swing, hand, sash-direction, width, lift-door, or fire-rating findings. Lift doors are sliding and measure 1.20 m nominal; the main entrance is a wide double-swing door.
The final counts of 88 doors and 148 windows exactly match the live model, and the agent openly disclosed the 0.6 m sill choice.
weaknesses: A single 0.604 m sill strategy was applied to nearly all windows, including the 19 guest/suite-envelope rooms and office-like uses; this is below the standard’s approximately 0.9–1.0 m expectation for bedrooms and offices.
Moving-leaf and sash sweep clearance against walls, fixtures, and adjacent leaves was not independently established; this remains not assessed rather than a failure.

Building-wide access status is unverified because 54 upper-floor rooms are reported as not linked to other floors, but this results from the disclosed reserved stair/lift starting-model condition and is not penalized in this opening-only review.

spec_violations.constraint: Window sill heights must suit the room use, approximately 0.9–1.0 m in bedrooms and offices.
spec_violations.what_happened: Almost all habitable-room windows use a uniform low sill of approximately 0.604 m, including guest-suite and office-like rooms.
spec_violations.evidence: Measured window bottoms were 0.604 m above the floor on all floor-1 windows and nearly all floor-2 and floor-3 windows; only four upper-corridor windows measured about 0.908 m.
